description: Read a past session from any AI agent and bring it into this conversation

<!-- generated by ectype skill install: command /ectype -->

Bring a past session into this conversation with the `ectype recall` command, run through your
shell tool. Needs the `ectype` command on PATH. Use it as `/ectype <id> [options]` (or
`/prompts:ectype`).

The user's input is: $ARGUMENTS
It is empty, a session id (any prefix), or words to search for, optionally followed by options
that `ectype recall` understands. Options typed there win over the defaults in ectype's
Settings -> Agent skill.

1. **Find it.** With no input, run `ectype list -n 20`, show the table, and ask which one. With
   words, run `ectype search '<words>'` first (one quoted pattern): it first summarises the sessions that are new
   or changed since the last search, then greps every summary ectype keeps, and says how many sessions it
   covered. If nothing matches, run `ectype list -n 60` and pick
   the row whose id starts with the input or whose title contains it. If several match, show only
   those and ask; never guess between two.

2. **Bring it in at the right depth.** Run `ectype recall <id>` with the options the user typed.
   The defaults start at the conversation alone: the user's and the agent's messages, a question
   the agent put to the user with the answer, and any message another session sent in (under
   `[PEER]`), with no tool calls. If that does not answer the question, re-read the part that does
   rather than the whole session: `--tools` adds every tool call by name, and `--tools --mode
   custom --cap 300` the first 300 tokens of each result too; `--thinking` adds the reasoning;
   `--start 40 --end 80` is a message range.
   With `--tools`, the tool-output mode is `--mode brief` (names only, the default), `--mode
   custom` (results capped at `--cap`) or `--mode full` (everything); a word the user typed such
   as `--brief` or `--full` means `--tools` with the matching `--mode`. `ectype recall --help`
   lists every option.

3. **It is remembered.** Unless `--no-summarize` was given, recall also saves the session's
   summary into ectype's own store, which is what `ectype search` reads next time; the command
   says so on stderr. Mention it in one line.

4. **Say what you took:** which session, which view, and roughly what it cost.

Do not run `ectype convert` or install anything unless the user asks in so many words: those
write into an agent's own store.
